title: Why Is MongoDB Stock Crashing and is it a Buying Opportunity? | MDB Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether MongoDB's post-crash price is a buying opportunity after its CEO was poached, which he calls a disruptive transition. He nonetheless stresses the underlying business is booming: $2.78B trailing revenue, operating cash flow at 24% of sales, R&D falling from 55% toward 28% of sales as scale builds, GAAP profitability expected by end-2027, and 20%+ growth guided over the next three years. Valuation is the constraint: at $386 the stock trades at 49x forward earnings, which he calls broadly fair versus peers, but his DCF fair value of $293 implies it is overvalued. He therefore reiterates the HOLD rating first set on Aug 20, saying he would upgrade only on a price nearer fair value or clearly better performance. Risks he flags include new-CEO missteps and growth slowing below 20%. Call made: MDB HOLD at $386 (stated), DCF fair value $293. Summary is based on the captions analysis recorded in the 15:00 run on 2026-10-12; auto-captions garble some names and figures.

calls.thesis: Reiterated Aug 20 rating: CEO poached, transition disruptive, but business booming (TTM rev $2.78B, 24% OCF/sales, 20%+ growth guided 3y); 49x forward P/E is fair but DCF FV $293 vs $386 = overvalued.
calls.bull_case: GAAP profitable by end-2027; expanding R&D scale (55%->28% of sales)
calls.bear_case: New CEO missteps; growth slows below 20%
